mynano.py.summary: A small Textual-based text editor with readline tab completion.
details: Opens the file given on the command line (or an empty buffer), provides quit, save and save-as actions plus a key binding list, and hooks ``readline`` with ``rlcompleter`` for the completion popup.

neg.py.summary: Invert the colours of image files in place.
details: Negates the RGB channels while keeping the alpha channel and the EXIF/ICC/DPI metadata, and replaces each file atomically (JPEG saved at quality 95). Files it cannot decode are reported and the exit status becomes 1.

new2old.py.summary: Render a ``setup.py`` from ``pyproject.toml`` for the detected build backend.
details: Reads the PEP 621 metadata plus the backend-specific tables (flit, hatchling, maturin, meson, pdm, poetry, scikit-build, setuptools), normalises the dependencies, authors, README and license and writes a ``setup.py`` that reproduces the project without ``pyproject.toml``.

noface.py.summary: Move the images that contain no face into a ``noface`` folder.
details: Runs the OpenCV Haar cascade (several frontal-face models) over the JPEG/PNG/BMP/TIFF/WebP files of the current directory, downscales large images, keeps the photos with a face in place and moves the rest to ``./noface``. The optional argument sets the worker count.

nolua.py.summary: List the sub-directories of the current directory that contain no Lua files.
details: Recursively checks each top-level folder for ``.lua`` sources and prints the names of the ones that have none. ``move_to_start`` copies such a folder into the vim plugin ``start`` directory and removes the original.

noneng_gcld3.py.summary: Detect the language of the text files below the current directory with gcld3.
details: Identifies each file with ``gcld3`` (falling back to ``py3langid`` for short samples) and prints the detected language with its confidence for every file whose language is not English.

noneng_langid.py.summary: Report every line of text that is not English, using py3langid.
details: Decodes each text file, classifies the lines above the minimum length with ``py3langid`` and prints the lines whose detected language is not English with their confidence, colourising the output and skipping binary extensions.

noneng_pycld2.py.summary: Detect the language of every text file with pycld2.
details: Walks the current directory (hidden entries ignored), guesses the language of each readable file with pycld2 and prints a table of file, language, probability and a short snippet.
noneng_pycld2.py.notes: Runs its scan at import time, so start it in the tree to inspect.

noneng_unicode_range.py.summary: Flag files that contain Arabic/Persian, CJK, kana or Hangul characters.
details: Checks every text file (binaries are skipped with ``binaryornot``) against the Unicode ranges of the major non-Latin scripts and reports the files with the detected scripts plus a short sample, optionally as JSON.

noreq.py.summary: Delete the ``Requires-Dist`` lines from package metadata and archives.
details: Processes ``METADATA``/``PKG-INFO``/``PKGINFO`` files and the same files inside wheels, zips and tarballs (including brotli/zstd/lz4/lzma compressed archives), removing the dependency declarations and logging every removed line to ``/sdcard/reqz.txt``.
noreq.py.notes: Destructive: it strips dependency metadata from the packages in the current tree.

noroot.py.summary: Remove the ``if [ $(...) -ne 0 ]; then exit 1; fi`` root checks from shell scripts.
details: Scans the executable or ``#!``-shell files below the current directory and deletes the matching guard blocks (typically the ``must run as root`` checks) with a regular expression, rewriting only the files that changed.

obf.py.summary: Obfuscate a shell script into three-character variables evaluated at the end.
details: Splits the script into three-character chunks, assigns each chunk to a generated variable name and finishes with a single ``eval`` that concatenates them, so the original text is no longer readable in the file.

ocr_ready.py.summary: Preprocess images so that Tesseract reads them reliably.
details: Deskews each scan, binarises it (OpenCV, scikit-image or Pillow depending on what is installed), removes noise and writes the cleaned image next to the original, in parallel. A quick Tesseract pass decides which variant is kept.

ocrpdf.py.summary: OCR every page of a PDF and print the extracted text.
details: Opens the document with PyMuPDF, renders each page through its OCR text page (English, 300 dpi) in a pool of four workers and joins the page texts with newlines.
